A Builder Is an Array: Growing It and Inserting at the Front Copy What Is Already There
setLength(0) Empties a Builder and Keeps Its Array
Two Builders Are Equal Only When They Are the Same Object

recorded.prompt:q-shared-buffer-separator: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shared-buffer-separator: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shared-buffer-separator: Lines 49-51 say each StringBuffer call such as append or length() locks only for that call and that another thread's text lands between calls, so the check-then-append is a compound action. Both threads can therefore read length 0 and skip the comma, which gives `cpumem`. Line 38's broken output shows the same effect, so option a is decided.
recorded.prompt:q-newest-first-view: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-newest-first-view: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-newest-first-view: Line 102 says insert(0, row) 'shifts every character already in the builder, on every call', and lines 105-110 show that doubling the rows quadrupled the time (20k->80k: 23->409 ms). So 4x the entries gives about 16x of 60 ms, roughly 1 s, which decides option a.
recorded.prompt:q-threadlocal-heap: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-threadlocal-heap: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-threadlocal-heap: Line 121 says setLength(0) 'only sets the length; the array the builder grew stays', line 130 says every thread that built something large 'keeps that much for as long as it lives', line 126 shows 160 MB held by idle pool threads, and line 182 says it 'holds its largest size for the life of its thread'. That decides option a.

recorded.pass:q-alert-dedupe: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-alert-dedupe: Lines 168-170 say StringBuilder inherits equals and hashCode from Object, so 'a HashSet<StringBuilder> used to drop duplicate messages keeps every one', and lines 161-165 show equals false and seen.contains(b) false for builders with equal text. That decides option a: two notifications.

recorded.prompt:q-shared-buffer-separator:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shared-buffer-separator:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shared-buffer-separator:b: Lines 49-50 say each call 'locks the buffer and sees what every earlier call wrote', which rules out a stale read. The problem is the gap between calls (lines 50-51), not visibility.
recorded.prompt:q-shared-buffer-separator:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shared-buffer-separator:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shared-buffer-separator:c: Lines 49-52 say per-call locking leaves the line unprotected and that 'no buffer method writes one', and line 38 shows 110,487 broken lines on a StringBuffer. Synchronized methods do not make check-then-append atomic.
recorded.prompt:q-shared-buffer-separator:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shared-buffer-separator:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shared-buffer-separator:d: Lines 64-67 refute 'only': lock coarsening merged the locks only after warm-up, -XX:-EliminateLocks broke 63-69 % of lines, and a passing test 'shows what this JIT did ... not what the language promises'. Partly true: the page confirms the JIT can merge adjacent locks (lines 64-65), so the option's mechanism is real but not guaranteed.
recorded.prompt:q-newest-first-view:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-newest-first-view:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-newest-first-view:b: Lines 73-82 say a builder keeps spare room and reallocates only when the text doesn't fit, growing to 2 x capacity + 2 (line 196), so it does not allocate a new array on every insert. Partly true: 'about a second' is the right figure with the wrong reason. Also, the page states the growth rule for appends ('when an append doesn't fit', line 80) and applies it to insert only by implication.
recorded.prompt:q-newest-first-view:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-newest-first-view:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-newest-first-view:c: Line 102 contrasts the two cases directly: 'Appending at the end copies only on growth', while insert(0, row) shifts every character on every call. The reason given is true of append, not insert, and lines 105-110 show quadratic rather than linear scaling.
recorded.prompt:q-newest-first-view:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-newest-first-view:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-newest-first-view:d: Line 102 (every insert at the front shifts all existing characters) and line 110 (quadratic, like += in unit 1.4.2) refute it. Partly true: each line is written into the builder once, but the page shows it is moved again by every later insert.

recorded.outcome:q-threadlocal-heap:c: Line 97 ('toString(), which always copies the text into a new String') and line 213 ('a new String on every call') say toString() does not hand over the builder's array.
recorded.prompt:q-threadlocal-heap:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-threadlocal-heap:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-threadlocal-heap:d: Refuted only indirectly. Line 97 says toString() copies the text, and line 139 says the 79-byte result String came from a builder of capacity 256, which implies the String is sized to its text, not the capacity. The page never states this outright.
recorded.prompt:q-alert-dedupe:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-alert-dedupe:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-alert-dedupe:b: Line 168 says the hashCode is Object's, and lines 168-170 present a content-based hash that changes with every append as the design Java avoided. The page implies but never states that the identity hash ignores appends. Also, in this stem each builder is finished before add, so mutation after insertion is not at issue.
recorded.prompt:q-alert-dedupe:c: the page and the question, and nothing else

recorded.outcome:q-alert-dedupe:c: Lines 163-165 show a.compareTo(b) is 0 while seen.contains(b) is false, so the HashSet does not use compareTo. The page shows this by example and never says outright that HashSet ignores compareTo.
